text: Aetna 270/271 eligibility requests began timing out at 09:14 on 7/21, climbing to a 61% timeout rate; other payer connections clean — Aetna-specific.

text: Root-cause hypothesis at 11:45: the endpoint began presenting a cert chain with a different intermediate CA than our pinned bundle — mTLS handshake failure, confirmed by packet capture at 12:30.
speaker: p_jake_osei

anchor.quote: Aetna rotated their intermediate CA without notice

text: Workaround live at 14:20: cached 271 responses served when ≤30 days old (labeled as cached), failed checks queued for overnight batch 270 — front desks functional again.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: Outage notice + workaround explanation went to all four affected clients at 14:47; no PHI exposure — connectivity only.
speaker: p_elena_vasquez

anchor.quote: went to all four affected clients at 14:47

text: Aetna's provider-tech line acknowledged the unannounced CA rotation at 16:50 ('planned maintenance, notification may not have reached all trading partners').
speaker: p_jake_osei

anchor.quote: acknowledged the CA rotation on their side

text: INC-2026-007 scope: 2,347 eligibility checks failed or queued between 09:14 and the 14:20 workaround; root cause confirmed as Aetna's unannounced intermediate-CA rotation vs our pinned bundle.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: Permanent fix deployed 7/23 in aetna.yaml: dual-bundle trust (legacy + new intermediate CA, fingerprint verified out-of-band) and exponential-backoff retry with jitter, reviewed by Marcus.
speaker: p_jake_osei

anchor.quote: dual-bundle trust carrying both the legacy and new intermediate CA

text: Verification + prevention: 24h post-fix error rate at 0.3% baseline; cert-chain monitoring (expiry + chain-change detection) shipped 7/24 for ALL payer mTLS endpoints.
speaker: p_jake_osei

anchor.quote: error rate back to baseline (0.3%, normal noise)

text: Overnight backfill processed all 2,347 queued eligibility checks (2,306 clean 271s); 41 members with cache older than 30 days were stale-flagged so ops re-verified before any claim release.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: The 41 stale-flagged claims were re-verified live on 7/23: 39 clean, 2 true coverage terminations caught before submission. No claim released on stale eligibility.
speaker: p_tom_reyes

text: aetna.yaml now runs dual-bundle mTLS trust (aetna-ca-2024 + aetna-ca-2026) with chain-change alerting, so unannounced CA rotations degrade gracefully instead of failing hard.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: Retry policy is exponential backoff (base 400ms, max 4 attempts, jitter) replacing the tight loop that amplified load during the outage.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: The cached-eligibility fallback is formalized in config: cached 271 served on live-check failure with a 24-hour freshness TTL, mandatory stale labeling, and overnight batch-270 queuing.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: Final incident numbers: ~5 hours degraded (09:14→14:20), 61% peak timeout rate, 2,347 checks failed/queued, four clients affected, zero stale-eligibility releases, zero PHI exposure.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: What didn't hold: no cert-chain monitoring existed (first signal was user-facing timeouts) and the tight-loop retry amplified load during the failure.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: DECISION (7/28): the cached-eligibility fallback becomes permanent and always-on — cached 271 on live-check failure, 24-hour freshness TTL, visible stale flag in the UI. Rationale: graceful degradation turned a lost clinic day into a 5-hour inconvenience; payer failures are a when, not an if.
speaker: p_jake_osei

text: Priya's caveat accepted into the decision: cached eligibility is a front-desk convenience, not a claims-release basis — scrub still requires a live-or-fresh check per SOP-001.
